thread:
Ava: heads up — the SLO expander in the detail card is rendering min/max slider, pool picker, and burst pill in a single compact row. on narrow modals the burst chip overlaps helper text. screenshot: https://redwood.app/s/ux/22455
Ravi: saw that. VoiceOver reads the helper text and then the overlapping chip, confusing flow order.
Noor: is this the compact table or the expanded detail card? can you attach the narrower screenshot?
design-bot: uploaded files: slo_expander_modal.png, slo_expander_ipad.png
Ava: detail card. uploaded two screenshots (1280x720 modal + iPad split). both show collisions when width < 720px.
Maya: quick UX thought — moving burst into an overflow menu reduces clutter but might hide an important control. not ideal for quick debugging.
Leo: agree with Maya. burst changes are operationally significant (affects latency/cost). should remain visible.
Ravi: what about responsive layout: keep min/max + pool on first row; push burst to second row when container width < 700px. preserves discoverability and avoids overlap.
Ava: that sounds good. keep spacing compact so it doesn't feel like a new section.
Noor: accessibility checklist: ensure focus order stays linear (min -> max -> burst -> pool -> save). add aria-describedby linking burst to a short explanation.
Maya: copy suggestion: don't rename the main label to "Burst (temp)". instead add a short tooltip: "Temporary extra GPUs for brief spikes — may increase cost." Keep label as "Burst".
Ravi: implementation note: flex-wrap + gap should do. slider should still expand full width. propose `display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:8px; align-items:center;` and give slider `flex:1 1 320px;` to avoid collapse.
Leo: i'll prototype a branch feature/slo-card-wrap and attach screenshots. will test 320px, 480px, 720px breakpoints.
design-bot: created branch feature/slo-card-wrap
Maya: microtest script for usability: 1) set min=1 max=4, 2) enable burst, 3) switch GPU pool. measure completion time and record any unexpected tab stops.
Ava: schedule a 15-20min microtest with 3 engineers after the prototype. Noor, can you run the accessibility check after that?
Noor: will do. i'll check keyboard nav, screen reader order, and ARIA labels. will report back Friday.
Ravi: :thumbsup:
Ava: thanks all — i'll update the product spec with the new responsive behavior and tooltip copy.
